title: Select and copy text in the Dashboard terminal on mobile

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: one check

**Verdict: Confirmed missing test path.**

An independent scratch observation shows the fault makes the promised behavior go wrong for an application that asks for button-event pointer tracking (xterm `vt200`), while the maintained checks examined pass with the fault and never open a terminal in that tracking mode.

## What was checked

- **Story.** `.planning/seeds/SEED-316-mobile-terminal-text-selection.md`, "Select and copy text in the Dashboard terminal on mobile" (SEED-316#select-and-copy-terminal-text-on-mobile). Plan `.planning/slice-plans/591-select-and-copy-terminal-text-on-mobile/PLAN.md`.
- **Revision.** `7981c2cce7c2dab3a354afb371040ac89a76a496` (detached scratch worktree of it; product code last changed in `fb62a8266`).
- **Promise.** Scope, "Swipe scrolls the output, whoever holds it": when the session's application has taken over the screen and scrolls its own output, the swipe scrolls that application's output the way a desktop wheel does at the touched place, deciding "by what the terminal reports about the application, not by host name." Plan decision 1 names the reported states: `modes.mouseTrackingMode` of `vt200`, `drag` or `any`.
- **Fault (one).** `dashboard/src/terminalTouchScroll.ts` line 5: `const wheelTracking: readonly string[] = ["vt200", "drag", "any"];` changed to `["drag", "any"]`. Fixtures and assertions untouched. The caller's suggested promise, fault, maintained check and command all held against the story and revision and were used unchanged.
- **Maintained checks examined.** Both tests of `dashboard/frontend-tests/agent-terminal-touch-application-scroll.spec.ts`: "a swipe scrolls an application that scrolls its own output, at the touched place, and leaves the draft alone" (application `selfScrollingApplication` in `dashboard/tests/support/terminalSubstituteApplication.ts`, which announces `?1049h ?1003h ?1006h`, tracking `any`) and "a swipe sends nothing to an application that took over the screen without taking the wheel" (`?1049h ?9h`, tracking `x10`).
- **Command.** From the scratch root: `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard -- frontend-tests/agent-terminal-touch-application-scroll.spec.ts --reporter=list --workers=2`.
- **Scratch witness (never committed, removed with the scratch worktree).** A copy of the first maintained test's arrangement (same MakeMe launch record, `openFrontendTerminalByTouch`, `selfScrollingApplication({ lines: 60, shown: 10 })`) whose opening has `?1003h` replaced by `?1000h`, so the terminal reports `vt200`. It types "draft", makes one five-and-a-half-row stroke toward earlier output, presses `!` and waits for the draft row to read `> draft!` (an observable event, no sleep), then prints what the page sent after the stroke and the first conversation line shown, and expects five button-64 wheel reports and the window five lines earlier. A copy is kept at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/de0e2361/tmp/ic-witness.spec.ts.txt`.

## Run observations

Machine load averages were 32 to 37 throughout. Logs are under `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/de0e2361/tmp/`.

1. **Baseline, maintained check, no fault** (`ic-run1-baseline.log`): 2 passed (28.9 s); both tests listed as run.
2. **Witness, no fault** (`ic-run2-witness-unfaulted.log`): 1 passed (21.3 s). Sent after the stroke: five `ESC[<64;20;1M` wheel reports, then `!`. First conversation line shown: 046 (from 051). The promised behavior works on the `vt200` path at this revision.
3. **Maintained check, with fault** (`ic-run3-maintained-faulted.log`, diff in `ic-fault.diff`): 2 passed (28.2 s), exit 0. Neither test failed.
4. **Witness, with fault** (`ic-run4-witness-faulted.log`): 1 failed, exit 1, on "one wheel report per whole row of travel": expected length 5, received 0. Sent after the stroke: only `!`. First conversation line shown: still 051. The swipe gave the application nothing and its output did not scroll.
5. **Restored, maintained check** (`ic-run5-restored.log`): 2 passed (21.2 s), exit 0.

- **Reach.** The faulted line is the swipe decision itself; the witness's change from pass (run 2) to fail (run 4) with only that line changed shows the faulted bundle was served and the decision was reached on the `vt200` path.
- **Wrong behavior.** Independently observed in run 4: no wheel report reached the session and the conversation window stayed at line 051, where the story promises the application's output scrolls.
- **Maintained proof.** The two examined tests open applications tracking `any` and `x10` only. No `vt200` (or `drag`) terminal is opened, so they do not exercise the wrong path; their passing in run 3 is not an assertion verdict on it.
- **Restoration.** The edit was undone by `git checkout -- dashboard/src/terminalTouchScroll.ts` from a shell trap. Afterward the scratch checkout was at `7981c2cce`, `git diff` was empty (same hash as the pre-probe empty diff), line 5 again read `["vt200", "drag", "any"]`, and the only status entry was the untracked witness file. Run 5 passed. The witness was then deleted (status clean) and the scratch worktree removed with `git worktree remove --force`; the path no longer exists and is not in `git worktree list`.

## Bounds

- The finding is bounded to the two tests of `agent-terminal-touch-application-scroll.spec.ts`. No other spec was run or searched; absence across the whole suite is not claimed.
- The omitted transition: a one-finger swipe on a terminal whose application reports `vt200` tracking (`?1000h`) sends one wheel report per row and scrolls the application's output. `drag` (`?1002h`) shares the list and was not faulted or witnessed here; one fault only.
- The witness ran in the frontend tier against the WebSocket substitute, in local Chromium with a phone touch viewport, as the maintained spec does. No real tmux or vim session was attached.

## Next proof action

Add journey proof for the omitted transition: a maintained page open of a swipe under button-event tracking (`?1000h`, and by the same reasoning `?1002h`) that expects wheel reports and the scrolled output. Test repair and routing stay with the caller.

## Prior disposition this matches

Recognition, not a new repair decision: the plan's slice 1 acceptance note already records "`vt200` and `drag` share the decision's list without a page open of their own," and `source-review.md` row S7.6 records mutations only for "!== none" and for removing "any". This probe adds the observation that the unprotected entry is load-bearing: removing it breaks the promised swipe for such an application and nothing examined notices.

## Notes for the caller

- The execution checkout was not edited, stashed, reset or cleaned by this check. At the end it showed ` M docs/dashboard-ux-ui-north-star.md`, which was not there in my first status reading and was not made by this check; its HEAD is still `7981c2cce`.
- Scratch setup: `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm`, `browser` and `check` each exited 0 on the first attempt with `/opt/homebrew/bin` first on `PATH` (Node v24.21.0, matching `.node-version`).

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** 99.6 s (measured) for the four runs where the Playwright runner printed its total: 28.9 + 21.3 + 28.2 + 21.2 s. The faulted witness run printed no total; its one test took 12.7 s by the runner and the command took 25.7 s by wall clock. Wall clock around all five commands, including npm and server start: 139.2 s (measured: 31.5 + 24.3 + 34.2 + 25.7 + 23.6 s), under load averages of 32 to 37.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable. No human took part in this check and nothing measured human time; reading this report is not measured.
- **Agent effort.** 17 tool calls (measured, counted from this run): 8 shell commands for lookup, setup and cleanup, 4 shell commands for the five test runs, 1 file read, 1 file write, 1 file edit, and 2 report-finisher calls, the second correcting this count. Token and price figures are unavailable: the agent has no reading of its own usage.
- **Scratch setup time** is included in the elapsed entry below, not in test runtime.



- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 303928 ms (measured), from 1794412012539 to 1794412316467 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

# Wrap-up disposition

- **Checked revision.** `7981c2cce7c2dab3a354afb371040ac89a76a496` (product code last changed in `fb62a826632bcfe2a6758f9728b46652a266aeae`). One probe: it does not protect the whole story.
- **Finding.** Confirmed missing test path: a one-finger swipe under button-event pointer tracking (xterm `vt200`, `?1000h`) is unprotected by the two tests of `dashboard/frontend-tests/agent-terminal-touch-application-scroll.spec.ts`. `drag` (`?1002h`) shares the decision's list and was not faulted.
- **Evidence.** The report above. In addition, at wrap-up the same scratch witness with `?1002h` passed in the execution checkout at `7981c2cce` (five wheel reports, first conversation line shown 046), so the delivered product works under all three tracking modes. A deliberate scratch fault is not a delivered defect; none was found.
- **Decision.** Routine test strengthening, queued as a separate bounded correction within wrap-up's authority. It matches a limitation the delivering execution recorded at slice 1 acceptance, so it does not call the delivered behavior into question and changes no priority beyond its own entry.
- **Follow-up.** `SEED-316#prove-swipe-under-button-event-tracking`, story in `.planning/seeds/SEED-316-mobile-terminal-text-selection.md#prove-swipe-under-button-event-tracking`, plan `.planning/slice-plans/596-prove-swipe-under-button-event-tracking/PLAN.md`, recorded ready and placed first in the Backlog list. No retrospective follow-up exists to precede it.
